title: Instagram users: Here’s how to stop Meta’s AI from using your photos
slides: Meta just started training AI on your Instagram photos.
The default setting is opt-out, not opt-in.
A single buried toggle controls everything.
You can turn it off in five seconds right now.
Check your privacy settings before tomorrow's update.
thread_text:
Meta just switched you to public. 

Instagram photos you posted years ago are now part of Meta’s AI training pipeline — unless you had already found the hidden setting.

The default was never your choice. 

Meta set the privacy toggle to “allow” for every user. You were opted into AI training without a notification or consent request.

One switch does it all. 

That single toggle controls every photo you’ve ever uploaded — past, present, and future. There’s no per-post or per-album control.

You can kill it in five seconds. 

Go to Settings > Privacy > “Allow Meta to use your photos for AI.” Flip it off. That’s it — no forms, no emails, no confirmation needed.

Check your settings now or lose the window. 

Meta pushes the update tomorrow. If you don’t toggle it off today, your photos become training data retroactively. Open Instagram and check this minute.
